newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rise after seesaw on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rise after seesaw on U.S. data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rose to new day's and multi-month peaks after briefly seesawing on U.S. data that traders decided did little to alter the low-inflation economic scenario.

Futures slipped then recovered when advance second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product grew at a 2.2-percent rate versus downwardly revised 4.9-percent first-quarter growth and compared to estimates for a 1.9-percent Q2 increase.
Both the implicit deflator and the price index grew at a 1.4-percent rate, the smallest quarterly increase in each inflation gauge in more than 30 years.
"The numbers were bullish," said one floor broker.
"The deflator was a pretty great number," added another broker. "Low inflation is what got this market going."
Traders also said the market got a lift from the American Production and Inventory Control Society business outlook index that rose to 53.0 in July versus forecasts for 53.3.
The first floor broker said the APICS data showed low inventory levels that reinforced the benign inflation picture.
They said the market glossed over weekly U.S. jobless data that fell 22,000 to 277,000 compared to forecasts for a 7,000 increase to 306,000 from the prior week's 299,000 level.
"The claims data - nobody knows how to read them anymore," said the first floor broker.
The market waits for Chicago purchasing managers July index, expected at 59.8 from 61.5 June. New York's purchasing management's diffusion index fell to 59.5 from 64.9 in June.

Brokers also said many buyers felt compelled to enter the market for bookkeeping purposes on the last day of the month, especially in light of the nearly six-point rally in September Treasury bond futures over the last month.
"We settled (the last day) in June at 111-02/32," the second broker said. "They're forcing some people in."

Some looked for September T-bond futures, if they return above intraday resistance at 116-25/32, to test the 117-10/32-12/32 area, roughly 6.25-percent cash equivalent yield. On pullbacks, 116-17/32 was seen as interim support.

At 0827 CDT/1327 GMT, Sept T-bonds rose 9/32 to 116-21/32, 10-year notes gained 7/32 to 110-31/32, muni-bonds added 7/32 to 122-09/32, December T-bills rose 0.015 to 94.890, and Eurodollars gained 0.020 to 94.205. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
